0158               
0159               ; While we don't mean to USE the console ROM, for interrupts we
0160               ; are forced to interface with some of it. We need these addresses
0161               ; to minimize what it does so we can maximize our use of scratchpad.
0162               ; While I'd like to use the cassette hook - requires only 10 instructions
0163               ; and only uses 6 words of scratchpad, we can't here because it
0164               ; loses the return address, meaning you can only use it if you
0165               ; know where your LIMI 2 is and interrupts are otherwise disabled. So
0166               ; we have to use the longer but more standard interrupt hook, which also
0167               ; reads VDP status for us (no choice).
0168               
0169      8379     intcnt              equ >8379   ; interrupt counter byte, adds 1 (from GPLWS r14) every frame
0170      837B     vdp_status          equ >837B   ; VDP status byte mirror
0171      83C2     intwsr1             equ >83c2   ; INT WS R1  - interrupt control flags - must be >8000
0172      83C4     intwsr2             equ >83c4   ; INT WS R2  - address of user interrupt routine (point to int_handler)
0173      83D6     intwsr11            equ >83d6   ; screen timeout counter - must be odd (init to 1, is inct every frame)
0174      83DA     intwsr13            equ >83da   ; INT WS R13 - used for interrupt call (word)
0175      83DC     intwsr14            equ >83dc   ; INT WS R14 - used for interrupt call (word)
0176      83DE     intwsr15            equ >83de   ; INT WS R15 - used for interrupt call (word)
0177      83F6     gplwsr11            equ >83f6   ; GPL WS R11 - return address to interrupt ROM (not used, but overwritten each int)
0178      83F8     gplwsr12            equ >83f8   ; GPL WS R12 - used for cassette test and interrupt hook test (zeroed each int)
0179      83FA     gplwsr13            equ >83fa   ; GPL WS R13 - used in my interrupt handler
0180      83FC     gplwsr14            equ >83fc   ; GPL WS R14 - flags used to detect cassette - must be >0108 (or at least >0020 clear)
0181      83FE     gplwsr15            equ >83fe   ; GPL WS R15 - base address of VDP for status read - must be >8C02

0470               ; Load sprite definitions: Sprite number in R4, CPU data in R0, count of sprites in R5 (MSB)
0471               ; Original: pointer = sprite number, temp = CPU address, a = number sprites
0472               ; Note: sprites are all expected to be double-size 16x16, 32 bytes each, so sprite char 1 is character 4
0473               ; Sprite pattern table at >3800
0474               define_sprite
0475 A1DA C20B  18     mov r11,r8          ; save return
0476 A1DC C080  18     mov r0,r2           ; Source data.
0477 A1DE C004  18     mov r4,r0           ; VRAM target.
0478 A1E0 0A50  26     sla r0,5            ; sprite number times 32 for bytes
0479 A1E2 0220  22     ai r0,>3800         ; add VDP base
     A1E4 3800     
0480 A1E6 C0C5  18     mov r5,r3		; Length.
0481 A1E8 0983  32     srl r3,8            ; make int
0482 A1EA 0A53  26     sla r3,5            ; count times 32
0483 A1EC 0300  22     limi 0              ; ints off
     A1EE 0000     
0484 A1F0 06A0  32     bl @LDIRVM          ; do the copy
     A1F2 A076     
0485 A1F4 0300  22     limi 2              ; ints on
     A1F6 0002     
0486 A1F8 0458  20     b *r8               ; back to caller
0487               
0488               ; Load character definitions: Char number in R1, CPU data in R2, count in R3 (MSB)
0489               ; Original: pointer = char number, temp = CPU address, a = number chars
0490               ; Note this loads the pattern three times if in bitmap mode (MODE&0x04)
0491               ; Pattern table at >0000
0492               define_char
0493 A1FA C20B  18     mov r11,r8          ; save return
0494 A1FC C080  18     mov r0,r2           ; source data
0495 A1FE C004  18     mov r4,r0           ; move input to scratch
0496 A200 0A30  22     sla r0,3            ; char number times 8 (VDP base is 0, so already there)
0497 A202 C0C5  18     mov r5,r3
0498 A204 0983  32     srl r3,8            ; make word
0499 A206 0A33  22     sla r3,3            ; count times 8
0500 A208 D160  30     movb @mode,r5       ; get mode flags
     A20A 834E     
0501 A20C 0245  22     andi r5,>0800
     A20E 0800     
0502 A210 1607  14     jne !1              ; not in bitmap mode, do a single copy
0503               
0504 A212 0300  22     limi 0              ; ints off
     A214 0000     
0505 A216 06A0  32     bl @LDIRVM3         ; do the triple copy
     A218 A090     
0506 A21A 0300  22     limi 2              ; ints on
     A21C 0002     
0507 A21E 0458  20     b *r8               ; back to caller
0508               
0509               !1
0510 A220 0300  22     limi 0              ; ints off
     A222 0000     
0511 A224 06A0  32     bl @LDIRVM          ; do the single copy
     A226 A076     
0512 A228 0300  22     limi 2              ; ints on
     A22A 0002     
0513 A22C 0458  20     b *r8               ; back to caller
0514               
0515               ; Load bitmap color definitions: Char number in R1, CPU data in R2, count in R3 (MSB)
0516               ; Original: pointer = char number, temp = CPU address, a = number chars
0517               ; Note: always does the triple copy. Color table at >2000
0518               define_color
0519 A22E C20B  18     mov r11,r8          ; save return
0520 A230 C080  18     mov r0,r2           ; source data
0521 A232 C004  18     mov r4,r0           ; move input to scratch
0522 A234 0A30  22     sla r0,3            ; char number times 8
0523 A236 0220  22     ai r0,>2000         ; add base address
     A238 2000     
0524 A23A C0C5  18     mov r5,r3
0525 A23C 0983  32     srl r3,8            ; make word
0526 A23E 0A33  22     sla r3,3            ; count times 8
0527 A240 0300  22     limi 0              ; ints off
     A242 0000     
0528 A244 06A0  32     bl @LDIRVM3         ; do the triple copy
     A246 A090     
0529 A248 0300  22     limi 2              ; ints on
     A24A 0002     
0530 A24C 0458  20     b *r8               ; back to caller
0531               
0532               ; Update sprite entry - copy data (4 bytes) to sprite table mirror at sprites
0533               ; R4 = sprite number, R5 = byte 1, r6 = byte 2, r7 = byte 3, r0 = byte 4 (all MSB)
0534               ; Original: A = sprite number, source data at sprite_data
0535               update_sprite
0536 A24E 0984  32     srl r4,8            ; make word
0537 A250 0A24  20     sla r4,2            ; x4 for address
0538 A252 0224  22     ai r4,sprites       ; sprite mirror address
     A254 2000     
0539 A256 DD05  32     movb r5,*r4+        ; move bytes
0540 A258 DD06  32     movb r6,*r4+        ; move bytes
0541 A25A DD07  32     movb r7,*r4+        ; move bytes
0542 A25C DD00  32     movb r0,*r4+        ; move bytes
0543 A25E 045B  20     b *r11
0544               
0545               ; SGN R0 - return 1, -1 or 0 as 16 bit
0546               _sgn16
0547 A260 C000  18     mov r0,r0       ; check for zero
0548 A262 1306  14     jeq !1          ; if yes, we're done
0549 A264 0240  22     andi r0,>8000   ; check for negative
     A266 8000     
0550 A268 1302  14     jeq !2          ; was not
0551 A26A 0700  14     seto r0         ; was negative, make it -1
0552 A26C 045B  20     b *r11          ; back to caller
0553               !2
0554 A26E 0580  14     inc r0          ; we know it was zero, and we want 1
0555               !1
0556 A270 045B  20     b *r11          ; back to caller
0557               
0558               ; 16-bit signed modulo. R1 % R2 = R0 - 9900 doesn't do signed divide
0559               ; original was stack%stack=YYAA
0560               ; Remainder is negative if the dividend was negative
0561               _mod16s
0562 A272 04C0  14     clr r0          ; make dividend 32-bit
0563 A274 C082  18     mov r2,r2       ; check divisor for zero
0564 A276 130A  14     jeq !1
0565 A278 0742  18     abs r2          ; make sure divisor is positive
0566 A27A C041  18     mov r1,r1       ; check sign of dividend
0567 A27C 1505  14     jgt !2          ; go do the faster positive version
0568               
0569 A27E 0741  18     abs r1          ; was negative, make it positive
0570 A280 3C02 128     div r2,r0       ; do the division => r2=quotient, r3=remainder
0571 A282 0501  14     neg r1          ; make remainder negative
0572 A284 C001  18     mov r1,r0       ; into r0
0573 A286 045B  20     b *r11
0574               
0575               !2
0576 A288 3C02 128     div r2,r0       ; do the division => r2=quotient, r3=remainder
0577 A28A C001  18     mov r1,r0       ; into r0
0578               !1
0579 A28C 045B  20     b *r11
0580               
0581               ; 16-bit signed divide. R1 / R2 = R0 - 9900 doesn't do signed divide
0582               ; original was stack/stack=YYAA
0583               ; Remainder is negative if the signs differ
0584               _div16s
0585 A28E 04C0  14     clr r0          ; make dividend 32-bit
0586 A290 C0C2  18     mov r2,r3       ; check divisor for zero
0587 A292 1308  14     jeq !1          ;
0588 A294 28C1  18     xor r1,r3
0589 A296 0742  18     abs r2
0590 A298 0741  18     abs r1          ; might as well make them positive now that we have copies
0591 A29A 3C02 128     div r2,r0       ; do the divide => r0=quotient, r1=remainder
0592 A29C 0243  22     andi r3,>8000   ; mask out sign bit
     A29E 8000     
0593 A2A0 1301  14     jeq !1          ; skip ahead to positive version
0594               
0595 A2A2 0500  14     neg r0          ; negate the result
0596               !1
0597 A2A4 045B  20     b *r11
0598               
0599               ; Random number generator - return in R0, (complex one uses R3,R4, simpler one only R0)
0600               ; Original output into YYAA
0601               random
0628               ; simpler one from dreamcast days...

     A2A8 834C

0631 A2AC 1702  14     jnc .rand1          ; jump if no 1

     A2B0 A2B8     
0633               .rand1
0634 A2B2 C800  30     mov r0,@lfsr        ; save the output
     A2B4 834C     
0635 A2B6 045B  20     b *r11
0636               rmask
0637 A2B8 B400         data >b400          ; mask for 16 bit
0639               
0640               ; Set SN Frequency: R0=frequency code, R2=channel command (MSB)
0641               ; Original: A=least significant byte  X=channel command  Y=most significant byte
0642               sn76489_freq
0643 A2BA C0C0  18     mov r0,r3

     A2BE 000F

     A2C6 8400

0649 A2CA 0240  22     andi r0,>003f
     A2CC 003F

0651 A2D0 D800  30     movb r0,@SOUND  ; most significant byte
     A2D2 8400     
0652 A2D4 045B  20     b *r11
0653               
0654               ; Set SN volume: R0=volume (MSB, inverse of attenuation), R2=channel command (MSB)

0656               sn76489_vol

     A2E0 8400

0832               
0833               ; this is where interrupts happen every frame
0834               ; Unlike a normal TI application, this one runs with interrupts ON,
0835               ; so all operations need to be sure to protect VDP address with LIMI 0,
0836               ; as well as any operations that might need to manipulate data managed
0837               ; by this interrupt. We enter via the normal user hook, so WP is on
0838               ; GPLWS, interrupts are off, and the VDP is already reset and status
0839               ; stashed on vdp_status (>837b). Our return address to the ROM is in
0840               ; r11, but we are NOT going to use it so that we don't need to reserve
0841               ; r8 for whatever nonsense it does. That means we need to load intws
0842               ; and RTWP ourselves at the end. We are on our own workspace so we
0843               ; don't have to worry about the main app's workspace.
0844               int_handler
0845               ; first copy the sprite table
0846 A48E 02E0  18     lwpi myintwp        ; separate safe workspace
     A490 8320     
0847               
0849 A492 C820  46     mov @>7ffe,@saved_bank  ; save bank switch page
     A494 7FFE     
     A496 8352     
0851               
0852 A498 020B  20     li r11,>005b        ; >1b00 with the write bit added, and byte flipped
     A49A 005B     
0853 A49C D80B  30     movb r11,@VDPWADR   ; SAL address
     A49E 8C02     
0854 A4A0 06CB  14     swpb r11
0855 A4A2 D80B  30     movb r11,@VDPWADR   ; going to copy the sprite table to VDP
     A4A4 8C02     
0856               
0857 A4A6 D2E0  30     movb @mode,r11
     A4A8 834E     
0858 A4AA 024B  22     andi r11,>0400      ; if bit >04 (inhibit flicker) is cleared, jump ahead to rotate
     A4AC 0400     
0859 A4AE 130A  14     jeq !4
0860               
0861 A4B0 04CB  14     clr r11             ; else we're going to just write it straight across
0862 A4B2 020C  20     li r12,128
     A4B4 0080     
0863 A4B6 020D  20     li r13,sprites
     A4B8 2000     
0864               !7
0865 A4BA D83D  40     movb *r13+,@VDPWDATA
     A4BC 8C00     
0866 A4BE 060C  14     dec r12
0867 A4C0 16FC  14     jne -!7
0868 A4C2 101B  14     jmp !5
0869               
0870               !4
0871 A4C4 D2E0  30     movb @flicker,r11   ; here we write it rotated every frame
     A4C6 834F     
0872 A4C8 022B  22     ai r11,>0400
     A4CA 0400     
0873 A4CC 024B  22     andi r11,>7f00
     A4CE 7F00     
0874 A4D0 D80B  30     movb r11,@flicker
     A4D2 834F     
0875 A4D4 06CB  14     swpb r11            ; make count
0876 A4D6 020C  20     li r12,32           ; count
     A4D8 0020     
0877               
0878               !6
0879 A4DA 022B  22     ai r11,sprites        ; this is still faster than separate incs
     A4DC 2000

0890               ; next read the joysticks - output needs to be 21xxLDRU - 1 and 2 are button and button2 respectively
0891               ; We don't have a button 2. We also need to read the keyboard and fill in key1_data. key2_data we
0892               ; will leave unused. Note key1_data expects Coleco-style 0-9,10-*,11-#,15=not pressed, but we can throw
0893               ; everything else as ASCII. We could do a split keyboard for 2 players, but I guess we'll leave it for now.

     A522 0006

1018               ; given a joystick read in r13, return bits in r12

1929               ; The stack is simulated using R10. It's not used in
1930               ; these functions but the compiled code will need it.
1931               ; To push: dect r10, mov r0,*r10
1932               ; To pop:  mov *r10+,r0
1933               ; However, for JSR a function is helpful - call this like:
1934               ; bl @jsr
1935               ; data <function_address>
1936               jsr
1937 A980 C3BB  30     mov *r11+,r14       ; get the jump address
1938 A982 064A  14     dect r10            ; make room on stack
1939 A984 C68B  30     mov r11,*r10        ; save return address
1940 A986 069E  24     bl *r14             ; new subroutine call, we can come back here
1941 A988 C2FA  30     mov *r10+,r11       ; get real return off stack - warning, all basic functions do this inline rather than return
1942 A98A 045B  20     b *r11              ; back to caller

1984               ;;; CVBasic code starts here
1985               	; 	' ==========================================================================
1986               	; 	' KEYSTONE KAPERS -- CVBasic, dual target TI-99/4A + ColecoVision.
1987               	; 	'
1988               	; 	' Garry Kitchen's 1983 Activision game. See DESIGN.md; 0 records the
1989               	; 	' research and the four places the sources disagree.
1990               	; 	'
1991               	; 	' Fifty seconds to run Harry Hooligan down inside a department store eight
1992               	; 	' screens wide and four levels tall, before he reaches the roof.
1993               	; 	'
1994               	; 	' THE THREE DECISIONS THIS FILE IS BUILT ON, all from DESIGN.md:
1995               	; 	'
1996               	; 	'   * THE VIEW FLIPS, IT DOES NOT SCROLL. Eight discrete screens; crossing
1997               	; 	'     an edge blits the next one. The per-frame budget never pays for the
1998               	; 	'     store at all -- RallyX repaints 576 chars every camera cell and had
1999               	; 	'     to have all its movement rewritten to survive that.
2000               	; 	'   * A SCREEN IS EXACTLY 256 PX, so an actor's x within its screen is one
2001               	; 	'     unsigned byte. No 16-bit world coordinate exists in this program.
2002               	; 	'   * ZERO PER-FRAME VDP READS. An actor's floor is an index into flry(),
2003               	; 	'     never a question asked of the screen, so the Ms. Pac-Man trap
2004               	; 	'     (actors x per-actor search) is absent by construction.
2005               	; 	'
2006               	; 	' The rules that shaped the code, all from CLAUDE.md 3A, because every one
2007               	; 	' of them fails SILENTLY:
2008               	; 	'
2009               	; 	'   * A plain variable is 8-BIT and a CONST over 255 TRUNCATES. Every
2010               	; 	'     name-table offset past row 7 is a #var or a bare literal.
2011               	; 	'   * Every #var comparison is UNSIGNED.
2012               	; 	'   * `<cmp> AND <cmp>` is miscompiled by the 9900 backend. Nested IFs.
2013               	; 	'   * A sprite at y=208 TERMINATES the sprite list. Hidden sprites go 209.
2014               	; 	'   * A GOSUB left by GOTO never pops. Death, catch and escape are STATES
2015               	; 	'     set in a routine and acted on at the top of the main loop.
2016               	; 	'   * MPY clobbers r0. Nothing here multiplies into an index -- the tables
2017               	; 	'     tsrc()/bdst()/lv8() exist precisely so that no multiply is needed on
2018               	; 	'     a path that reads the result back.
2019               	; 	' ==========================================================================
2020               	;
2021               	; 	' ---------------------------------------------------------------- BANKING
2022               	; 	' THE ART AND THE STORE MAP LIVE IN ROM BANK 1 ON THE TI. The fixed area
2023               	; 	' is 24,336 bytes -- three 8,112-byte loader pages -- and unbanked this
2024               	; 	' program filled 24,304 of them, so there was no room left for anything at
2025               	; 	' all. `linkticart` does not warn when you exceed it; it silently discards
2026               	; 	' the top of the image, and what goes missing is whatever sits nearest the
2027               	; 	' end, usually a DATA block rather than code. Nothing errors.
2028               	; 	'
2029               	; 	' WHAT IS SAFE TO BANK. Everything moved here is read at SETUP (the
2030               	; 	' DEFINE CHAR / DEFINE SPRITE calls) or on a screen crossing (the template
2031               	; 	' blit and the escalator's phase tables) -- and, because there is exactly
2032               	; 	' ONE data bank and it is selected ONCE at startup and never switched, it
2033               	; 	' stays mapped for the life of the program. The rule in CLAUDE.md 3A is
2034               	; 	' about SWITCHING inside a frame or under the vblank ISR; with a single
2035               	; 	' permanently-selected bank there is no switch to miss. A missed
2036               	; 	' BANK SELECT would return bytes from the wrong page with no error at
2037               	; 	' build or run time, which is why there is only one and it is set before
2038               	; 	' anything reads from it.
2039               	; 	'
2040               	; 	' BANK ROM 128 sizes ColecoVision's Megacart mapper, NOT the TI cart --
2041               	; 	' that comes from how many bank files the assembler emits -- and it is
2042               	; 	' one of only four values the compiler accepts (128/256/512/1024).
2043               	; 	' The whole thing is gated on TI994A: the Coleco build is Z80 and roughly
2044               	; 	' half the size, so it neither needs banking nor wants to become a
2045               	; 	' Megacart image.
2046               	; 	#if TI994A
2047               	; 	BANK ROM 128
2048               	; 	#endif
2049               	; 	CONST SPRHID = 209		' NOT 208 -- 208 terminates the sprite list
2050      00D1     const_SPRHID	equ >00d1
2051               	;
2052               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------------------- geometry
2053               	; 	' A band is 5 rows: 4 rows of air (32 px) over one floor slab. Standing
2054               	; 	' Kelly is 16 px, so headroom is 16 px and the jump apex is 14 -- two
2055               	; 	' short of the ceiling, because an arc that bonks is silently truncated.
2056               	; 	' 4 px/frame = 240 px/s. At 2 it was not merely sluggish, it was
2057               	; 	' ARITHMETICALLY TOO SLOW: the climb is three traverses = 6,144 px, which
2058               	; 	' at 2 px/frame is 51 seconds of pure running against a 50-second clock,
2059               	; 	' before a single obstacle, escalator ride or catch. At 3 it is 34 s --
2060               	; 	' and 34 s was still wrong, for a reason a per-actor speed check cannot
2061               	; 	' see: HARRY'S CLIMB IS ALSO 34 s (DESIGN.md 4a). Kelly being 1.5x faster
2062               	; 	' bought nothing, because Harry's route is two thirds the length of
2063               	; 	' Kelly's -- he spawns beside floor 2's escalator and effectively skips a
2064               	; 	' traverse. A chase resolves on PATH / SPEED, not on speed, and the two
2065               	; 	' quotients were equal, so pursuit on foot could never close. At 4 the
2066               	; 	' climb is 25 s against Harry's 45, and the elevator buys back more.
2067               	; 	CONST WALKSP = 4		' px per PASS -- the old unit, kept only for
2068      0004     const_WALKSP	equ >0004
2069               	; 					' the checkers' arithmetic and the comments
2070               	; 					' that quote it. Nothing moves by it now.
2071               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS OF A PIXEL PER FRAME, which is what he actually walks by.
2072               	; 	'
2073               	; 	' HIS OLD BEST-CASE SPEED, MADE CONSTANT -- not his old average. WALKSP was
2074               	; 	' 4 px per loop PASS, so what he actually did depended on the screen: 104 px/s
2075               	; 	' on a light one at 26 passes/s, 80 px/s on the lift and escalator screens at
2076               	; 	' 20. Matching the MEASURED AVERAGE of 23.8 passes/s gave 95.6 px/s (102/64),
2077               	; 	' which is the same average and an 8% loss on exactly the screens a chase
2078               	; 	' spends most of its time crossing -- the crook was already per-frame and did
2079               	; 	' not change, so the ratio that decides the chase quietly dropped. Played, it
2080               	; 	' read as only just catching him on the last screen.
2081               	; 	'
2082               	; 	' 111/64 is 104.1 px/s: his best case, everywhere. He is now at least as fast
2083               	; 	' as he ever was on any screen rather than faster on some and slower on
2084               	; 	' others, and the chase margin goes from 10.6 s to 17.3 s.
2085               	; 	CONST KWALK64 = 111
2086      006F     const_KWALK64	equ >006f
2087               	; 	' The bounce phase, in sixty-fourths of a phase per frame. 32 phases at
2088               	; 	' 25/64 per frame is 1.37 s an arc, against the 1.35 s one phase per pass
2089               	; 	' gives at 23.8 passes a second.
2090               	; 	CONST BOUNCE64 = 25
2091      0019     const_BOUNCE64	equ >0019
2092               	; 	CONST XWALL = 232		' furthest left edge at the store's east wall
2093      00E8     const_XWALL	equ >00e8
2094               	; 	CONST XWALW = 8			' nearest left edge at the west wall
2095      0008     const_XWALW	equ >0008
2096               	; 	CONST STANDH = 24		' Kelly standing -- TWO SPRITES tall
2097      0018     const_STANDH	equ >0018
2098               	; 	' KELLY DUCKED. It was 8 px, which is not a crouch -- it is a squash, with
2099               	; 	' no room to draw a figure bending in a DIRECTION. 11 px is, and the
2100               	; 	' biplane is raised to match (obh below, and the hitbox in coll_obst):
2101               	; 	' with the plane at 16..22 an 11 px crouch passes five pixels under it and
2102               	; 	' a 24 px standing Kop does not. The apex is 14, so a jump still cannot
2103               	; 	' clear it either -- the plane stays the one obstacle that must be ducked.
2104               	; 	'
2105               	; 	' AND 11 IS THE CEILING, not a preference. Duckable means the obstacle
2106               	; 	' clears the crouch, jumpable means it clears under the apex; raising the
2107               	; 	' crouch raises the duckable floor, so past 11 a band of beach-ball
2108               	; 	' heights is neither. A sweep of every crouch height against every ball
2109               	; 	' hitbox puts the limit at 11, and shrinking the ball does not move it --
2110               	; 	' the apex is what binds. assets/checkball.py fails the build on it.
2111               	; 	CONST DUCKH = 11		' Kelly ducked -- bent over, not squashed
2112      000B     const_DUCKH	equ >000b
2113               	; 	CONST CATCHR = 12		' catch / hit radius, centre to centre
2114      000C     const_CATCHR	equ >000c
2115               	;
2116               	; 	' Kelly states
2117               	; 	CONST ST_RUN = 0
2118      0000     const_ST_RUN	equ >0000
2119               	; 	CONST ST_JUMP = 1
2120      0001     const_ST_JUMP	equ >0001
2121               	; 	CONST ST_DUCK = 2
2122      0002     const_ST_DUCK	equ >0002
2123               	; 	CONST ST_ESC = 3		' riding an escalator -- no input, invincible
2124      0003     const_ST_ESC	equ >0003
2125               	; 	CONST ST_ELEV = 4		' inside the car     -- no input, invincible
2126      0004     const_ST_ELEV	equ >0004
2127               	;
2128               	; 	' obstacle kinds, matching assets/genstore.py
2129               	; 	CONST OB_CART = 1
2130      0001     const_OB_CART	equ >0001
2131               	; 	CONST OB_BALL = 2
2132      0002     const_OB_BALL	equ >0002
2133               	; 	CONST OB_RADIO = 3
2134      0003     const_OB_RADIO	equ >0003
2135               	; 	CONST OB_PLANE = 4
2136      0004     const_OB_PLANE	equ >0004
2137               	;
2138               	; 	' sprite patterns (DEFINE SPRITE index n -> pattern n*4)
2139               	; 	' THE VDP CANNOT MIRROR A SPRITE -- there is no flip bit -- so every actor
2140               	; 	' that runs both ways carries a second set of frames. assets/genart.py
2141               	; 	' generates the left ones from the right ones so the two directions are
2142               	; 	' guaranteed identical.
2143               	; 	' KELLY AND HARRY ARE 24 PX -- a 16 px top sprite with the top half of a
2144               	; 	' second sprite below it. A band gives 32 px of air plus the 7 px of the
2145               	; 	' ceiling row under its 1 px slab line = 39 px, and 24 + the 14 px jump is
2146               	; 	' 38. The apex CANNOT be reduced to buy room: at 10 px the ball's jump and
2147               	; 	' duck windows stop overlapping and a dead band opens (DESIGN.md 5a).
2148               	; 	'
2149               	; 	' The two sprites never share a scanline, so a band still costs Kelly 1 +
2150               	; 	' Harry 1 + two obstacles = four per line.
2151               	; 	' Pattern numbers are genart.py's SPRITES order x 4. Move one there and
2152               	; 	' this table must move with it -- nothing checks the correspondence.
2153               	; 	' SPRITE PATTERNS, laid out by genart.py so the selection code is three
2154               	; 	' statements rather than two mirrored branches. Everything that FACES comes
2155               	; 	' in a RIGHT block and then a LEFT block of the same shape, so changing
2156               	; 	' facing is one fixed offset; the LEGS do not face and are shared.
2157               	; 	CONST P_KHAT = 0		' Kelly RIGHT: hat, black
2158      0000     const_P_KHAT	equ >0000
2159               	; 	CONST P_KFACE = 4		'              face, skin
2160      0004     const_P_KFACE	equ >0004
2161               	; 	CONST P_KBODY = 8		'              tunic, arms down
2162      0008     const_P_KBODY	equ >0008

2437               	; 	' HOW FAR THE SECOND HAZARD ON A FLOOR TRAILS THE FIRST, in pixels.
2438               	; 	'
2439               	; 	' THERE ARE ONLY TWO SAFE ANSWERS AND THE SCREEN ONLY FITS ONE OF THEM.
2440               	; 	' Kelly closes on an oncoming ball at WALKSP + 2 = 6 px a pass, so:
2441               	; 	'
2442               	; 	'   <= 54 px   ONE JUMP CLEARS BOTH -- the arc holds its 14 px apex for
2443               	; 	'              nine passes, which is 54 px of closing distance
2444               	; 	'   >= 168 px  he can LAND BETWEEN them -- the arc is airborne for 28
2445               	; 	'              passes, which is 168 px
2446               	; 	'
2447               	; 	' Anything in between is the dangerous middle: too far to clear together,
2448               	; 	' too close to land between. The gap shipped at 46 px west of the lift and
2449               	; 	' 70 px east of it -- 46 is inside the first window and 70 is squarely in
2450               	; 	' that middle, which is the asymmetry that got reported.
2451               	; 	'

2453               	; 	' a bigger gap moves the second hazard TOWARD the player: at 168 px it
2454               	; 	' starts within 72 px of the wall he walks in through, and at 176 it lands
2455               	; 	' essentially on top of him with no time to read it. That was tried and it
2456               	; 	' is worse than the bug it replaced.
2457               	; 	'
2458               	; 	' So 48 -- inside the one-jump window with margin, uniform on every screen,
2459               	; 	' and it leaves the nearer hazard at least 192 px away at entry. The pair
2460               	; 	' is one obstacle taken with one well-timed jump, which is also what the
2461               	; 	' original's paired hazards read like. assets/checkspace.py checks all of
2462               	; 	' it and checkspace_test.py proves it rejects 70 and 176 alike.

2468      0055     const_ELOPEN	equ >0055
2469               	; 					' built from other CONSTs is exactly the
2470               	; 					' folded-constant trap in CLAUDE.md 3A
2471               	;
2472               	; 	' escalator boarding zones, in CENTRE-x pixels
2473               	; 	' ESCALATOR BOARDING ZONES, IN PIXELS, AND THEY TRACK THE ART.
2474               	; 	' The flight is drawn as four rows of two characters stepping two columns
2475               	; 	' per row: west runs cols 1-2 (top) down to 7-8 (foot), east runs 29-30
2476               	; 	' (top) down to 23-24 (foot). These zones ARE those columns x8. When the
2477               	; 	' escalator art changed from a filled triangle to a stepped flight the
2478               	; 	' foot moved, and a boarding zone left where it was would put the player
2479               	; 	' on a staircase that is not under them -- no error, just a floor that
2480               	; 	' teleports you when you walk over an empty patch of it.
2481               	; 	' THESE ARE THE DRAWN STEPS, in screen pixels. The flight is fifteen
2482               	; 	' characters wide: its foot tread sits at x 95-103 (west) and 152-160
2483               	; 	' (east), its head tread at 23-31 and 224-232. An actor rides between
2484               	; 	' those, so the numbers here are the ART's, and moving the art without
2485               	; 	' moving them puts the rider beside the escalator rather than on it.
2486               	; 	' THE RIDER STANDS ON A STEP, and everything about the ride follows from
2487               	; 	' WHICH ONE. The staircase is a straight line -- a step 4 px higher is 8
2488               	; 	' px further along it -- so one number, the step's height above the floor
2489               	; 	' being left, fixes both the rider's x and the rest of the ride:
2490               	; 	'
2491               	; 	'     west  klx = 99 - 2*height        east  klx = 140 + 2*height
2492               	; 	'
2493               	; 	' The bottom step is 4 px up, so a rider walking on boards at klx = 91
2494               	; 	' (west) or 148 (east); the head step is 40 up, so the ride ends at 19 or
2495               	; 	' 220. Those are the ART's numbers -- the foot tread is drawn at x 95-103
2496               	; 	' west and 152-160 east, the head tread at 23-31 and 224-232 -- so moving
2497               	; 	' the art without moving these puts the rider beside the staircase.
2498               	; 	'
2499               	; 	' THE PHASE MATTERS. The steps climb 1 px a frame and the animation runs
2500               	; 	' four 1 px phases, so the bottom step is 4 + escp px up, not 4. Boarding
2501               	; 	' without that term leaves the feet up to 3 px out of register with the
2502               	; 	' tread and the whole ride drifts, which is exactly what "he floats
2503               	; 	' beside the steps" looked like.

2520      0032     const_TIMEL	equ >0032
2521               	; 	' FRAMES PER TIMER UNIT. 120, not 60, and this is not cosmetic -- it is
2522               	; 	' what makes a round finishable. Everything that MOVES in this game is
2523               	; 	' paced per loop PASS, and the loop runs about 25 passes a second, so
2524               	; 	' Kelly's 4 px a pass is ~100 px/s (the reference's Kelly is 102, so the
2525               	; 	' speeds match). The timer, though, is paced by the frame DELTA -- real
2526               	; 	' wall-clock time. At 60 frames a unit the round was 50 real seconds
2527               	; 	' while Kelly's route to the roof takes about 72, so the clock ran out
2528               	; 	' before either of them could get there and every round ended on a
2529               	; 	' timeout. checkchase.py hid it by assuming 60 passes a second; it now
2530               	; 	' models the real rate.
2531               	; 	CONST TICKFR = 120
2532      0078     const_TICKFR	equ >0078
2533               	; 	' NINE TIMER UNITS -- not ten, and not nine seconds. Every source says a
2534               	; 	' cart, ball or radio costs "9 seconds", and what they mean is the number
2535               	; 	' on the HUD, because that is what the manual calls seconds. So the
2536               	; 	' DISPLAYED count drops by 9. A unit is about two real seconds
2537               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 0m), which makes one careless cart cost roughly eighteen --
2538               	; 	' close to a fifth of the round, and the reason the refractory latch
2539               	; 	' below matters so much.
2540               	; 	CONST HITPEN = 9		' timer units a cart / ball / radio costs
2541      0009     const_HITPEN	equ >0009
2542               	; 	' HOW LONG A HIT SOUNDS, IN LOOP PASSES -- and therefore how long the
2543               	; 	' store stands still for one. The two are the same number on purpose:
2544               	; 	' the freeze is meant to last exactly as long as the noise, so a change
2545               	; 	' to one that did not move the other would leave either a silent pause
2546               	; 	' or a sound playing over a resumed game. Passes, not frames, because
2547               	; 	' both counters are spent once per pass in sfx_tick and the main loop.
2548               	; 	CONST HITSND = 20

2550               	; 	CONST HITREF = 45		' frames before the SAME obstacle can charge

2552               	; 					' again. See coll_obst -- clearing the latch
2553               	; 					' on the first non-overlapping frame is not
2554               	; 					' enough, because a bouncing ball leaves
2555               	; 					' contact between bounces.
2556               	;

2558               	; 	DIM flry(4)			' floor surface y, by level
2559               	; 	DIM #bdst(4)			' band name-table offset, by level

2562               	; 	DIM jarc(32)			' the jump arc: 30 frames, apex 14
2563               	; 	DIM msk(8)
2564               	;
2565               	; 	' EIGHT obstacle slots -- TWO per band, and that number is forced.
2566               	; 	'
2567               	; 	' The VDP shows four sprites per scanline and DROPS the rest by slot
2568               	; 	' order; it does not flicker them, they simply are not there. Three per
2569               	; 	' band was sized against Kelly alone (1 + 3 = 4) and forgot that HARRY
2570               	; 	' can be on that band too -- and when he is, the fifth sprite on his
2571               	; 	' scanline is the highest-numbered obstacle, which vanishes while still
2572               	; 	' being solid. An invisible thing that costs nine seconds is the worst
2573               	; 	' failure in the game and it only happens when the crook is next to you,
2574               	; 	' which is exactly when you are not looking at the floor.

2899               	;
2900               	; 	' THE ONE AND ONLY BANK SWITCH THE PROGRAM EVER MAKES, and it happens
2901               	; 	' here, before the first frame.
2902               	; 	'
2903               	; 	' There are two data banks now. Bank 1 holds everything read while the
2904               	; 	' game is running -- sprite and store art, the templates, the lookup
2905               	; 	' tables -- and it is selected at the end of this routine and never
2906               	; 	' changed again, so every VARPTR/PEEK read in the program is reading a
2907               	; 	' page that is permanently mapped. That is the property that makes
2908               	; 	' banking safe here: a missed BANK SELECT returns bytes from the wrong
2909               	; 	' page with no error at build or run time, so the safest number of
2910               	; 	' switches during play is none.
2911               	; 	'
2912               	; 	' Bank 2 exists to hold data that is read ONCE, at setup, and never
2913               	; 	' again. The font is exactly that: two DEFINEs copy it into VRAM and
2914               	; 	' nothing reads font_bits or font_col for the rest of the run. So it can
2915               	; 	' live on a page that is mapped for the length of those two statements.
2916               	; 	'
2917               	; 	' IF THIS EVER FAILS IT FAILS LOUDLY. Select the wrong bank here and the
2918               	; 	' font is garbage on the title screen, immediately and unmistakably --
2919               	; 	' which is the same diagnostic the font used to provide by staying out of
2920               	; 	' the banks altogether, recovered for free.
2921               	; 	#if TI994A
2922               	; 	BANK SELECT 2
2923 ABA8 04E0  34 	clr @>6008
     ABAA 6008     
2924               	; 	#endif
2925               	;
2926               	; 	DEFINE CHAR 32,59,font_bits
2927 ABAC 0204  20 	li r4,32
     ABAE 0020     
2928 ABB0 0205  20 	li r5,15104
     ABB2 3B00     
2929 ABB4 0200  20 	li r0,cvb_FONT_BITS
     ABB6 602A     
2930 ABB8 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     ABBA A980     
2931 ABBC A1FA     	data define_char
2932               	; 	' Without this the font keeps whatever CVBasic left in the colour table --
2933               	; 	' white on transparent -- which over a green store made the HUD unreadable.
2934               	; 	'
2935               	; 	' THIS WAS A VPOKE LOOP AND IT WAS THE SLOWEST THING IN THE BOOT: 1,416
2936               	; 	' writes of one constant, paced by 24 WAITs, which is what made the title
2937               	; 	' fill in visibly instead of appearing. DEFINE COLOR does the same job in a
2938               	; 	' single call with interrupts off, and it writes all three screen thirds
2939               	; 	' itself -- define_color always takes the LDIRVM3 triple-copy path, which is
2940               	; 	' also why esc_deck_col and floor0_colour below CANNOT use it: they patch
2941               	; 	' one third each.
2942               	; 	'
2943               	; 	' The table is 472 identical bytes (genfont.py emits it beside the glyphs).
2944               	; 	' It reads as waste and is not: it lives in the data bank, which had 860
2945               	; 	' bytes spare, while the loop it replaced cost time in the one place the
2946               	; 	' player is made to wait.
2947               	; 	DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col
2948 ABBE 0204  20 	li r4,32
     ABC0 0020     
2949 ABC2 0205  20 	li r5,15104
     ABC4 3B00     
2950 ABC6 0200  20 	li r0,cvb_FONT_COL
     ABC8 6202     
2951 ABCA 06A0  32 	bl @jsr
     ABCC A980     
2952 ABCE A22E     	data define_color
2953               	;
2954               	; 	' AND THE TITLE'S DISPLAY FACE, WHICH IS HERE FOR THE SAME REASON THE
2955               	; 	' FONT IS. Forty characters -- ten letters, four cells each -- drawn at
2956               	; 	' 16x16 so the game's name reads as a name rather than as a line of body
2957               	; 	' text. It is 640 bytes of pattern and colour and bank 1 had 370 free, so
2958               	; 	' it could not go there; it did not need to, because it is read ONCE, by
2959               	; 	' these two statements, and never again.
2960               	; 	'
2961               	; 	' Loading it inside the bank-2 window the font already opens means the
2962               	; 	' program still makes exactly ONE bank switch in its life.
2963               	; 	' IN TWO PIECES, AND THE SPLIT IS NOT TIDINESS. The character table has
2964               	; 	' 0..31, 91..95 and 182..207 free -- sixty-three codes, but the longest
2965               	; 	' run is thirty-two and the face needs forty. Loading it as one block at
2966               	; 	' 182 ran it into the RADAR CANVAS at 208, and S and T came out as the
2967               	; 	' scanner's green diagonals on a screen with no radar on it.
2968               	; 	'
2969               	; 	' The arguments come from titleface.FREE_RUNS; gentitle.py prints them
2970               	; 	' into the top of titlefont.bas and checkchars.py verifies them.

3292               	;
3293               	; 	' THE JUMP ARC IS A TABLE, not integration. That makes the 14 px apex a
3294               	; 	' property of the data rather than of a fixed-point velocity that has to
3295               	; 	' be tuned, and it keeps every comparison in the jump 8-bit and unsigned.
3296               	; 	' DESIGN.md 5a depends on the apex being exactly 14.
3297               	; 	'
3298               	; 	' THIRTY FRAMES WITH NINE OF THEM AT THE APEX. The first version was 24
3299               	; 	' frames that touched 14 for only four, which made every jump a timing
3300               	; 	' test rather than a decision -- you had to leave the ground on exactly
3301               	; 	' the right frame or clip the thing you were jumping. Widening the
3302               	; 	' plateau rather than raising the apex keeps the ball arithmetic in
3303               	; 	' DESIGN.md 5a intact (the apex is what that depends on) while making the
3304               	; 	' window forgiving: the player still has to CHOOSE to jump, but no longer
3305               	; 	' has to be frame-perfect about it.
3306               	; 	' THE ARC IS A TABLE, not thirty assignments -- each of those compiled to
3307               	; 	' several bytes of code, and the fixed area is the binding budget.
3308               	; 	#jat = VARPTR jarc_tbl(0)

3361 AF16 0450  20 	b *r0
3362               	;
3363               	; 	' THE FONT'S COLOUR TABLE WAS 472 BYTES OF ONE REPEATED VALUE, which is a
3364               	; 	' fifth of what the fixed area had left. DEFINE COLOR copies such a table
3365               	; 	' out of ROM into all three screen thirds; writing the constant straight
3366               	; 	' into the colour table does the same job for the price of a loop, and
3367               	; 	' the loop runs once, at boot.
3368               	; 	'
3369               	; 	' The colour table is at >2000 and the VDP mirrors it once per screen
3370               	; 	' third, >800 apart. Both numbers were read out of the GENERATED assembly
3371               	; 	' -- define_color's `ai r0,>2000` and LDIRVM3's `ai r0,>0800` -- rather
3372               	; 	' than assumed, because a wrong base here would paint over the pattern
3373               	; 	' table and the failure would look like corrupt artwork.
3374               	; 	'
3375               	; 	' Paced: a few hundred VDP writes in one frame are silently dropped.
3376               	; 	' THE SCANNER'S COLOURS ARE THREE BLOCKS REPEATED SIXTEEN TIMES EACH, so
3377               	; 	' the table shipped 384 bytes to say 24 bytes' worth. Same trick as the
3378               	; 	' font: write the colour table directly. >2000 is the colour table's base
3379               	; 	' and >800 the stride between screen thirds -- the same layout DEFINE COLOR
3380               	; 	' walks for us in setup_font, which this cannot use because it is cheaper to
3381               	; 	' expand 24 bytes here than to ship 384 in the bank.
3382               	; 	' NOTHING IS UNDER THE GROUND FLOOR, SO NOTHING SHOULD BE GREEN THERE.
3383               	; 	' A floor bar is five pixels of yellow over three of the green air
3384               	; 	' belonging to the floor BELOW it (see SLAB), which is right for three of
3385               	; 	' the four bars and wrong for the last one: below floor 0 there is no
3386               	; 	' floor, only the scanner, and the green read as a strip of shop with
3387               	; 	' nothing in it.
3388               	; 	'
3389               	; 	' NO NEW CHARACTER IS NEEDED, BECAUSE THE COLOUR TABLE HAS THREE COPIES
3390               	; 	' -- one per eight screen rows -- and the bands land such that each bar
3391               	; 	' sits in a different third:
3392               	; 	'
3393               	; 	'     band 0 roof   rows  1-5    bar row  5   third 0
3394               	; 	'     band 1        rows  6-10   bar row 10   third 1
3395               	; 	'     band 2        rows 11-15   bar row 15   third 1
3396               	; 	'     band 3 GROUND rows 16-20   bar row 20   third 2
3397               	; 	'
3398               	; 	' so recolouring SLAB in third 2 alone reaches the ground floor's bar and
3399               	; 	' nothing else. The same third also holds the scanner, but the scanner
3400               	; 	' does not use these characters. This is the same mechanism that once hid
3401               	; 	' a bug for months (CLAUDE.md 3A, the blanked-in-one-third note) used
3402               	; 	' deliberately for once.
3403               	; 	'
3404               	; 	' Only the three bottom lines change, and only their BACKGROUND: SLAB has
3405               	; 	' no ink there and SLABE's brick keeps its grey.
3406               	; floor0_colour:
3407               cvb_FLOOR0_COLOUR
3408               	; 	' TWO CHARACTERS, THE SAME THREE SCAN LINES, ONE ROUTINE. Both blocks
3409               	; 	' were written out in full and differed only in which character and which
3410               	; 	' colour byte -- eleven statements twice, including the multiply-by-eight
3411               	; 	' done by doubling (`*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, which clobbers r0,
3412               	; 	' CLAUDE.md 3A).
3413               	; 	f0c = CH_SLAB

3618               	; 	' ======================================================================
3619               	; 	' TITLE
3620               	; 	' ======================================================================
3621               	; 	' DRAWING THE TITLE AND WAITING ON IT ARE TWO ROUTINES, because the boot
3622               	; 	' does something between them: the rest of setup runs while this is on
3623               	; 	' screen. They used to be one, which is why the title could not be shown
3624               	; 	' until everything was ready.
3625               	; 	' THE TITLE IS A DISPLAY LIST IN A ROM BANK, not twelve PRINT ATs.
3626               	; 	'
3627               	; 	' CVBasic embeds a string literal in the FIXED AREA, which is the only
3628               	; 	' budget that cannot be grown -- linkticart writes exactly three loader
3629               	; 	' pages and discards the rest, and they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
3630               	; 	' >A000 rather than cart ROM. 190 characters of title text were sitting
3631               	; 	' in the scarcest place in the program.
3632               	; 	'
3633               	; 	' AND THE REAL POINT IS WHAT IT COSTS NEXT TIME. With the text in a
3634               	; 	' table, changing what the title says or where it sits is an edit to
3635               	; 	' assets/gentitle.py and a rebuild. It costs bank bytes, of which there
3636               	; 	' are thousands, instead of fixed-area bytes, of which there are tens.
3637               	; 	'
3638               	; 	' The table is `row, col, length, bytes...` with 255 to end. ROW AND
3639               	; 	' COLUMN rather than a 16-bit screen offset, because reassembling one
3640               	; 	' from two bytes needs a multiply, and on the TMS9900 MPY clobbers r0 --
3641               	; 	' the next line that reads the product's variable gets the HIGH word
3642               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). Five doublings have no such hazard and are smaller.

3760               	;
3761               	; 	' NO ALPHA LOCK CALIBRATION, AND THERE USED TO BE ONE.
3762               	; 	'
3763               	; 	' The premise was that ALPHA LOCK shares a line with the joystick's
3764               	; 	' VERTICAL axis, so a latched key reports a direction that is never
3765               	; 	' released -- fatal here, where down is the duck and up is the lift. The
3766               	; 	' guard sampled the axis for forty frames before listening and then
3767               	; 	' ignored any direction that had been held for essentially all of them.
3768               	; 	'
3769               	; 	' IT WAS REMOVED BECAUSE THE PREMISE DOES NOT HOLD UP.
3770               	; 	'
3771               	; 	'   * CLAUDE.md claimed every other game here dodged the problem by not
3772               	; 	'     reading up/down. EIGHT of them do read it -- Adventire, Astiroids,
3773               	; 	'     HardHatMack, Ms. Pac-Man, RallyX, Structris, UFO, Bust-A-Bobble --
3774               	; 	'     and not one has a calibration or has ever shown the fault.
3775               	; 	'   * It never fired on the machine this is developed on: the notice it
3776               	; 	'     prints when it detects a stuck axis has never appeared.
3777               	; 	'   * The original evidence was that the game "came up and would not
3778               	; 	'     start" -- and the first version BLOCKED until the axis cleared. That
3779               	; 	'     symptom is indistinguishable from the several input bugs since found
3780               	; 	'     and fixed for real: keys arriving at a screen that was not listening
3781               	; 	'     yet. The diagnosis was probably one of those.
3782               	; 	'
3783               	; 	' It also cost two bugs of its own: forty frames of a drawn but deaf title
3784               	; 	' screen, which swallowed the first digit of 8-3-8, and a wrong theory
3785               	; 	' about keyboard noise that led to a filter which ate real presses.
3786               	; 	'
3787               	; 	' If a stuck axis ever does appear it will be obvious -- the player will
3788               	; 	' duck or ride the lift without asking -- and the guard is in the history.
3789               	;

3799               	; 	' finished, and completely deaf. A player types 8-3-8 into that window and

3939               	;
3940               	; 	' 8-3-8 IS EDGE-TRIGGERED AND ANY STRAY DIGIT RESETS IT (see title_wait).
3941               	; 	'
3942               	; 	' It used to read cont1.key raw every pass and test only for the digit it
3943               	; 	' wanted next. That worked -- but only because 8-3-8 ALTERNATES, so holding
3944               	; 	' 8 cannot advance past the first step. It is an accident of the sequence
3945               	; 	' rather than a design, and it had two costs: 8,5,3,9,8 opened this page as
3946               	; 	' readily as 8,3,8, and a key that READS as held for many frames got a free
3947               	; 	' walk through the state machine.
3948               	; 	'
3949               	; 	' That second one is not hypothetical on this machine. ALPHA LOCK shorts a
3950               	; 	' keyboard line -- and Classic99 defaults to invertcaps, so it reads DOWN
3951               	; 	' with the host's Caps Lock UP -- and this page was reached twice from
3952               	; 	' single keypresses while testing an unrelated change.
3953               	; 	'
3954               	; 	' The reset is the DEFAULT rather than a test for a particular wrong digit:
3955               	; 	' Bust-A-Bobble resets only on a stray 3 and still lets 8,5,3,8 through.
3956               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------------- 838 setup page

3962               	; 	' ONE PROMPT AT A TIME, NOTHING ELSE ON THE SCREEN, AND NO NUMBERS UNTIL
3963               	; 	' THEY ARE TYPED. There is no heading and no instructions: a page showing

4641               	;
4642               	; 	' ======================================================================
4643               	; 	' DRAWING THE STORE -- four blits, once per screen crossing
4644               	; 	' ======================================================================
4645               	; 	' This is the whole cost of the flip, and it is paid on a discrete event
4646               	; 	' rather than every frame. RallyX's pan repaints 576 chars every time the
4647               	; 	' camera moves one cell; this repaints 640 about once every two seconds
4648               	; 	' of running.
4649               	; 	' SPRITES OFF BEFORE THE BLIT, NOT AFTER IT. This routine WAITs between
4650               	; 	' bands -- one band a frame, because a burst of VDP writes past a few
4651               	; 	' dozen in one frame is silently dropped -- so painting the new screen
4652               	; 	' takes several frames, and for all of them the OLD screen's actors and
4653               	; 	' obstacles were still sitting on top of it. Following Harry through a
4654               	; 	' seam showed him and every cart from the floor he had just left,
4655               	; 	' standing on a shop that was assembling itself underneath them.
4656               	; 	'
4657               	; 	' They are put back by the normal draw on the same pass, so the crossing
4658               	; 	' reads as a cut rather than as a dissolve with ghosts in it.
4659               	; 	' EACH BAND IS FINISHED BEFORE THE FRAME IT IS DRAWN IN ENDS, and the
4660               	; 	' bands go TOP DOWN. Both halves of that matter.
4661               	; 	'
4662               	; 	' The blit paints the template -- shelves, pillars and all -- and the
4663               	; 	' radios and prizes then take out the fixtures they stand in. Those two
4664               	; 	' used to be four frames apart: all four bands blitted with a WAIT
4665               	; 	' between them, and only afterwards the clearing. So every screen change
4666               	; 	' showed its counters and beams for several frames and then erased them,
4667               	; 	' which reads as the shop flickering rather than as it being drawn.
4668               	; 	'
4669               	; 	' TOP DOWN because a band's beam tops are stamped into the SLAB ROW OF
4670               	; 	' THE BAND ABOVE. Going bottom-up, band 1's blit would paint over the
4671               	; 	' beam tops band 0 had just put there. Going top-down the band above is
4672               	; 	' always already drawn, so everything a band needs -- its own cells and
4673               	; 	' the row it borrows overhead -- is final by the time its WAIT arrives.
4674               	; 	'
4675               	; 	' `3 - dq` rather than `FOR dlv = 3 TO 0 STEP -1`: dlv is an unsigned
4676               	; 	' byte, so counting down past zero wraps to 255 and the loop never ends

4788               	;
4789               	; 	' A SUPPORT BEAM HAS TO REACH THE FLOOR IT HOLDS UP, AND THAT FLOOR IS
4790               	; 	' NOT IN ITS OWN BAND. A beam fills its band's four air rows, so its top
4791               	; 	' pixel sits under the slab row of the band ABOVE -- and a slab row is
4792               	; 	' five pixels of bar over three of green (see SLAB), so the beam stopped
4793               	; 	' three pixels short of the bar on every storey. It read as a beam that
4794               	; 	' misses the floor, which is exactly what it was.
4795               	; 	'
4796               	; 	' It cannot be drawn into either template. The beam belongs to the band
4797               	; 	' below and the row belongs to the band above, and the two templates are
4798               	; 	' chosen independently per screen, so no template knows both. So the
4799               	; 	' band blits go down first and the tops are stamped afterwards, from a
4800               	; 	' per-template column table -- the same shape as the escalator's head cap.
4801               	; 	'
4802               	; 	' Bands 0 and 1 only. Band 2's top row is the ROOF DECK, which is grey
4803               	; 	' over grey with no green to bridge, and the roof itself has no band
4804               	; 	' above it at all.
4805               	; 	' BANDS 0 TO 2 -- ALL THREE SHOPPING FLOORS. It used to stop at 1,
4806               	; 	' because band 2's ceiling is the ROOF DECK and the deck had no green
4807               	; 	' under it: a beam there already ran straight into grey and needed
4808               	; 	' nothing. Giving the roof its three green rows (so the lift shaft stops
4809               	; 	' under it, like every other floor) took that away, and the top floor's
4810               	; 	' beams started falling three pixels short.
4811               	; 	'
4812               	; 	' So the roof gets its own version of the stamp. A beam HOLDS THE ROOF

5349               	; 			' AND HOW MANY FLOORS CARRY ONE AT ALL. The gates above
5350               	; 			' decide what KIND a hazard is; this decides whether the
5351               	; 			' floor has one.

5353               	; 			' The kind-arrival rule downgrades anything that has not
5354               	; 			' arrived yet to a beach ball rather than leaving the floor
5355               	; 			' empty, so that a floor is never bare -- and the effect on
5356               	; 			' Krook 1 was a ball on all FOUR floors of every populated
5357               	; 			' screen. All four bands are on screen at once, so that is
5358               	; 			' four identical balls in view at all times, which is not
5359               	; 			' what "merely a few beach balls" describes.
5360               	; 			'
5361               	; 			' Per-band count was never the problem: only one slot is
5362               	; 			' live until Krook 6. It is the number of OCCUPIED FLOORS,
5363               	; 			' and it had no ramp at all.
5364               	; 			'
5365               	; 			' Floors 1 and 3 stay clear on Krook 1, floor 1 joins on
5366               	; 			' Krook 2, and the roof on Krook 3. ALTERNATING rather than
5367               	; 			' clearing the top or bottom half, so the empty floors do
5368               	; 			' not stack into a visibly dead region that reads as a bug
5369               	; 			' -- and the ROOF is last, because that is where the round

5472               	; 			' PER KIND, not one global speed (see start_krook).
5473               	; 			' THE SPEED IS A PROPERTY OF THE KIND, and obs() only ever
5474               	; 			' held a copy of it -- set from the kind here, zeroed for a
5475               	; 			' radio below, and read in one place. upd_obst derives it
5476               	; 			' from obk() instead, which is 8 bytes of RAM back and one
5477               	; 			' fewer thing that can disagree with itself.
5478               	; 			' THEY COME FROM THE FAR SIDE. Kelly walked into this screen
5479               	; 			' from one edge, so the obstacles start at the OTHER edge and
5480               	; 			' run toward him. Crossing a seam then always presents an
5481               	; 			' ONCOMING stream, never a set of backs he has to catch up
5482               	; 			' with -- and it means the direction he is travelling is
5483               	; 			' always the direction the danger comes from.
5484               	; 			'
5485               	; 			' The table's x becomes a stagger from that edge rather than
5486               	; 			' an absolute position, and the slot index spreads them out
5487               	; 			' so they arrive in sequence instead of as one wall.
5488               	; 			'
5489               	; 			' THE SECOND ONE IS A FIXED DISTANCE BEHIND THE FIRST, AND
5490               	; 			' THAT DISTANCE IS SET BY THE JUMP.
5491               	; 			'
5492               	; 			' It used to be `(lx AND 63) + 64` -- a masked byte out of
5493               	; 			' the placement table plus a constant -- so the gap between
5494               	; 			' the two hazards was whatever those two bytes happened to
5495               	; 			' differ by. Measured across the five populated screens it
5496               	; 			' came out 46, 46, 70, 70, 70 px. Screens 2 and 4 flank the
5497               	; 			' elevator, so the store had a visibly tighter pair on one
5498               	; 			' side of it than the other, which is exactly how it was
5499               	; 			' reported from play.
5500               	; 			'
5501               	; 			' Both numbers are too small, which is the real fault. Kelly
5502               	; 			' closes on an oncoming hazard at WALKSP + the hazard's own
5503               	; 			' speed = 6 px a pass, and a jump lasts about 30 passes, so
5504               	; 			' a jump eats ~120 px of closing distance. At 46 or 70 there
5505               	; 			' is NO screen where he can land between the two: he clears
5506               	; 			' the first and comes down on the second.
5507               	; 			'
5508               	; 			' HAZGAP is that distance with margin. The first hazard
5509               	; 			' still lands where the table puts it, so the placement
5510               	; 			' variety is unchanged; only the pairing is now a fact about

5512               	; 			' assets/checkspace.py measures it and fails the build.
5513               	; 			' THE SECOND SLOT IS MEASURED FROM THE FIRST, not from its

5602               	; 			' THE BALL IS ON THE GROUND WHEN HE GETS TO IT.
5603               	; 			'
5604               	; 			' The bounce phase used to be `lx AND 31` -- a byte out of
5605               	; 			' the placement table, which is to say arbitrary. Run onto
5606               	; 			' a screen and the first ball might be at the bottom of its
5607               	; 			' arc, where a jump clears it, or at the top, where it has
5608               	; 			' to be ducked, and nothing on the way in told you which.
5609               	; 			' Sometimes you could keep running and jump it; sometimes
5610               	; 			' the same approach at the same speed could not be jumped
5611               	; 			' at all. That is not difficulty, it is a coin toss.
5612               	; 			'
5613               	; 			' So the phase is worked BACKWARDS from the meeting. He
5614               	; 			' closes 4 px a pass and the ball 2, so they meet in
5615               	; 			' (gap / 6) passes; the phase advances one a pass and wraps
5616               	; 			' at 32, so seeding it with the NEGATIVE of that lands it on
5617               	; 			' phase 0 -- the ground -- exactly as they arrive.
5618               	; 			'
5619               	; 			' The gap is the same either way round: he enters at one
5620               	; 			' wall and the ball starts `stag` in from the other, so it
5621               	; 			' is 232 - stag whichever direction the floor runs.
5622               	; 			'
5623               	; 			' It stays forgiving rather than exact. The arc is flat near
5624               	; 			' the bottom, so anything within eight passes either side is
5625               	; 			' still under the jump; and it only holds for an unbroken
5626               	; 			' run, which is the case the player is entitled to read off
5627               	; 			' the screen. Duck, stop or take a hit and everything after
5628               	; 			' is out of step again -- which is the game.

7974               	;
7975               	; 	' THE VICTROLA, AS CHARACTERS. It never moves, so a sprite spent a
7976               	; 	' scan-line slot on something that can be painted once when the screen is
7977               	; 	' drawn -- and at one 16x16 sprite it could only ever be one colour and
7978               	; 	' one size. Four cells is twice the area for no sprite at all.
7979               	; 	'
7980               	; 	' It stands ON the slab, so it fills the band's rows 2 and 3; row 4 is
7981               	; 	' the floor bar itself and draw_prizes uses row 3 for a collectible,
7982               	; 	' which is why the two never share a screen (genstore keeps prizes off
7983               	; 	' the screens that carry hazards).
7984               	; 	'
7985               	; 	' rdall = 1 paints all four cells, 0 repaints only the top-right one --
7986               	; 	' the pulse. Same address arithmetic either way, so the two cannot drift.
7987               	; 	' A BEAM TOP HANGS OUT OF THE FLOOR ABOVE, and the beam it belongs to has
7988               	; 	' just been taken away. `beam_tops` stamps SLABP -- the floor bar with the
7989               	; 	' support carried up through its lower three pixel rows -- into the slab
7990               	; 	' row above every pillar, and it runs BEFORE the radios and prizes are
7991               	; 	' placed. Clearing a pillar's own cells therefore left three grey pixels
7992               	; 	' dangling from the ceiling with nothing under them.
7993               	; 	'
7994               	; 	' TESTED, NOT ASSUMED: only SLABP is put back to SLAB. The row above the
7995               	; 	' top shopping floor is the ROOF DECK, a different character altogether,
7996               	; 	' and writing a floor bar over it would punch a hole in the roof.
7997               	; 	' A SHELF RUN IS FIVE CELLS WIDE and a radio covers two, so one standing
7998               	; 	' on a counter punched a hole through its middle and left the ends either
7999               	; 	' side -- the same incoherence the dangling pillar had, and worse, because
8000               	; 	' a counter reads as one object. The whole unit goes: walk outward along
8001               	; 	' the band's row 2 while the cell is still a shelf top, clearing it and
8002               	; 	' its bottom half together.
8003               	; 	'
8004               	; 	' Bounded at eight steps. The runs are five, so eight is slack rather
8005               	; 	' than a guess -- and an unbounded walk would run off the end of the row
8006               	; 	' if the name table ever held something unexpected.
8007               	; wipe_shelf:
8008               cvb_WIPE_SHELF
8009               	; 	wsn = 8

8693               	; 	' the bounce advanced once per PASS -- so whether a jump cleared a ball

8695               	; 	' checkball.py proves was exact only at fdv = 1.

8698               	; 	' game: a 32-phase arc would drop from about 1.35 s to 0.55 s, balls

8700               	; 	' 25/64 of a phase per frame is 23.4 phases a second, against the 23.8 it

8702               	; 	' clear it.

8921               	; 	' ONE STEP OF A FRACTIONAL SPEED, FOR WHOEVER IS MOVING.
8922               	; 	'
8923               	; 	' `pacc` in and out, `psp64` in (sixty-fourths of a pixel per FRAME),
8924               	; 	' `pspd` out (whole pixels this pass). CVBasic has no locals, so the caller
8925               	; 	' stages its own accumulator in and takes it back out; that costs four
8926               	; 	' statements against the fourteen this used to be, written out per actor.
8927               	; 	'
8928               	; 	' Harry had the only copy. Kelly, the hazards and the bounce phase all need
8929               	; 	' the same thing -- everything the round clock judges has to advance by
8930               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAMES, or the loop rate becomes a difficulty dial and where the
8931               	; 	' player stands decides the outcome (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
8932               	; 	'
8933               	; 	' TWO DRAINS CAP THE STEP AT 2 PER FRAME whatever psp64 says (CLAUDE.md
8934               	; 	' 3A: N drains cap the speed at N, and the surplus leaks into a byte that
8935               	; 	' wraps). Every caller is under that: Kelly 102/64 = 1.6, the fastest
8936               	; 	' hazard 76/64 = 1.2, Harry 57/64 = 0.9, the bounce phase 25/64 = 0.4.
8937               	; 	'
8938               	; 	' FIVE FRAMES, AND THREE WAS TOO FEW. At 2 px a frame five frames is 10 px,
8939               	; 	' and to skip a position window an actor must start outside it on one side
8940               	; 	' and land outside on the other, which needs 12. Three was the original bug
8941               	; 	' in miniature: the lift screen runs at almost exactly 20 passes a second,
8942               	; 	' which IS fdv = 3, so every hitch there lost a frame. The clamp exists for

9424               cv573
9425               	;
9426               	; 	' THE SIXTEENTH-PIXEL ACCUMULATOR. hx is one unsigned byte per screen
9427               	; 	' (2), so there is nowhere to keep a fraction -- the fraction lives here
9428               	; 	' and is spent as whole pixels. THREE IFs, not a loop and not a divide:
9429               	; 	' `%` and `/` both compile to a real TMS9900 DIV (CLAUDE.md 3A) and this
9430               	; 	' runs every pass.
9431               	; 	'
9432               	; 	' THE NUMBER OF DRAINS IS A CEILING ON THE SPEED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE
9433               	; 	' POINT OF THIS COMMENT. Each IF can spend one whole pixel, so N drains
9434               	; 	' cap hspd at N px per pass NO MATTER WHAT hsp64 SAYS. The invariant is:
9435               	; 	'
9436               	; 	'     hacc is under 16 on entry, and hsp64 is at most 48,
9437               	; 	'     so hacc is under 64 here and three drains always suffice.
9438               	; 	'
9439               	; 	' KEEP hsp64 <= 48. This was quarter-pixels with TWO drains and the same
9440               	; 	' invariant written the same way -- "hsp4 is at most 8, so it can never
9441               	; 	' need a third" -- and it was correct until somebody set hsp4 = 9 without
9442               	; 	' re-reading it. The crook then ran at a flat 2.0 px/pass while every
9443               	; 	' comment, the design table and assets/checkchase.py all said 2.25, and
9444               	; 	' the surplus quarter leaked into hacc and wrapped the byte every 256
9445               	; 	' passes. Nothing failed; he simply arrived two thirds of a screen short
9446               	; 	' of his own escape. checkchase.py now counts these IFs and refuses a
9447               	; 	' speed the drains cannot deliver.
9448               	; 	'
9449               	; 	' 7, NOT 6, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED. Tracked off the reference video
9450               	; 	' (DESIGN.md 4a), the 2600's Kelly covers 0.40 screen widths a second and
9451               	; 	' its Harry 0.193 -- a ratio of 2.07. At hsp4 = 6 ours was 2.67, and the
9452               	; 	' crook visibly strolled. 7 brings it to 2.29. 8 would match the original
9453               	; 	' exactly and cannot be used: Kelly's route here is 1.95x Harry's, so a

9557               	; 	' HE WALKS BY REAL TIME, NOT BY LOOP PASS -- one accumulate-and-drain per
9558               	; 	' ELAPSED FRAME rather than per pass. Everything that moves here used to be
9559               	; 	' per pass while the CLOCK is paced by the frame delta, so a busy screen
9560               	; 	' slowed Harry in real seconds and the clock did not slow with him: the
9561               	; 	' same uninterrupted escape finished with nine timer units in hand from a
9562               	; 	' light screen and none at all from the lift screen, decided by where the
9563               	; 	' player happened to be standing. Now he covers the same ground per second
9564               	; 	' wherever anybody is (DESIGN.md 0f-ter).
9565               	; 	'
9566               	; 	' A LOOP, NOT A MULTIPLY. `*` compiles to a real TMS9900 MPY, and reading a
9567               	; 	' 16-bit variable straight after one returns the product's HIGH word
9568               	; 	' (CLAUDE.md 3A). fdv is 1..3 here, so this is at most three adds.
9569               	; 	'
9570               	; 	' SIXTY-FOURTHS, AND ONLY TWO DRAINS -- both fall out of accumulating per
9571               	; 	' FRAME instead of per pass. He covers under a pixel a frame, so two drains
9572               	; 	' are ample where the per-pass version needed three; and the finer unit is
9573               	; 	' what makes the speed tunable at all. In sixteenths one step was about six
9574               	; 	' SECONDS of his route, so nothing landed near the buzzer; in sixty-fourths
9575               	; 	' it is about one and a half. Keep hsp64 <= 128: hacc is under 64 on entry,
9576               	; 	' so 64 + 128 stays inside a byte and two drains always suffice.
9577               	; 	'
9578               	; 	' AND THE STEP IS CLAMPED TO THREE FRAMES' WORTH, WHICH IS NOT A DETAIL.
9579               	; 	' Two tests sample his position once a pass and neither interpolates:
9580               	; 	'
9581               	; 	'   ARRIVAL   `hdx < 6` around the escalator or the roof door -- an ELEVEN
9582               	; 	'             pixel window. A step over 10 px can jump clean across it and
9583               	; 	'             he never arrives at all.
9584               	; 	'   THE CATCH `hdd < CATCHR` is 12, a 23-wide band, and Kelly closes 4 of
9585               	; 	'             it himself -- so Harry over ~18 px could pass through the Kop
9586               	; 	'             between two passes without either sample being inside it.
9587               	; 	'
9588               	; 	' The clamp and the drains live in pace_step now, with the reasoning; the
9589               	; 	' numbers above are what sized them. Measured: TIME 02 on the lift screen
9590               	; 	' against TIME 04 on a light one when the clamp was 3, and 00 against 09
9591               	; 	' before any of this.
9592               	; 	'
9593               	; 	' The ESCALATOR RIDE is deliberately untouched: it returns above this,
9594               	; 	' clocked one step per pass to stay locked to the moving staircase. A rider
9595               	; 	' advanced by the frame delta either drifts off the treads or makes the
9596               	; 	' steps run backwards (CLAUDE.md 3A, DESIGN.md 0f). It is about 3% of his

9598               	; 	'
9599               	; 	' `hanim` still advances by hspd and is still an ODOMETER -- pixels

10039               	;
10040               	; 	' ======================================================================
10041               	; 	' COLLISIONS -- pure arithmetic against RAM, no VDP reads
10042               	; 	' ======================================================================
10043               	; 	' Kelly's box is [kfh, kfh + kh) above the slab; an obstacle's is
10044               	; 	' [ohb, oht). The ball's inset hitbox is what makes 8..10 avoidable both
10045               	; 	' ways -- without it there is a height at which the ball can be neither
10046               	; 	' jumped nor ducked, and an unavoidable hazard is not difficulty.
10047               	; 	' ONE HIT PER CONTACT, WITH A REFRACTORY PERIOD.
10048               	; 	'
10049               	; 	' The overlap test is true on every frame the player is touching
10050               	; 	' something, so with no latch at all one clumsy cart charges nine seconds
10051               	; 	' several times over -- and what the player sees is the clock jumping by
10052               	; 	' 27, from which the only available conclusion is that the penalty is
10053               	; 	' broken.
10054               	; 	'
10055               	; 	' A latch that clears on the first non-overlapping frame is still not
10056               	; 	' enough, and the case that breaks it is the BOUNCING BALL: it rises off
10057               	; 	' the player between bounces, which is a genuine loss of contact, so a
10058               	; 	' player standing still under one is taxed on every single bounce while
10059               	; 	' being given no opportunity to do anything about it. Technically two
10060               	; 	' collisions; in play, one situation.
10061               	; 	'
10062               	; 	' So obht() is a countdown, not a flag. A hit sets it to HITREF; it ticks
10063               	; 	' down only while the player is CLEAR, and the same obstacle cannot charge
10064               	; 	' again until it reaches zero. Contact holds the count up, so parking
10065               	; 	' inside something never earns a second penalty either.
10066               	; coll_obst:
10067               cvb_COLL_OBST
