10371               	; 	' THE FLOOR CLEARS WHEN YOU ARE HIT, and stays clear until you re-enter
10372               	; 	' the screen. Nine seconds is a heavy penalty on a fifty-unit clock, and
10373               	; 	' taking it while still standing among the things that charged it -- with
10374               	; 	' a second hazard 48 px behind the first -- is how one mistake becomes
10375               	; 	' three. Clearing the row makes the penalty a single event you can walk
10376               	; 	' away from.
10377               	; 	'
10378               	; 	' BOTH SLOTS, WHATEVER IS IN THEM. Radios used to be exempt: they are
10379               	; 	' CHARACTERS stamped into the name table rather than sprites, so zeroing
10380               	; 	' the kind would have stopped them colliding while leaving them plainly
10381               	; 	' visible on the shelf, and a fixture that is still there has to still be
10382               	; 	' there. That was a reason to UNDRAW them, not a reason to keep them --
10383               	; 	' and it left the one hazard that cannot leave on its own as the only one
10384               	; 	' the mercy did not cover. haz_off now takes the characters with it.
10385               	; 	'
10386               	; 	' NOTHING RESTORES IT HERE. load_band repopulates the band from the
10387               	; 	' template, and it runs only on a seam crossing or a round start, so
10388               	; 	' "until the screen is re-entered" costs no state and no timer: leave and
10389               	; 	' come back and the hazards are simply placed again.
10390               	; 	'
10391               	; 	' THE CALL ITSELF IS IN THE MAIN LOOP, at the end of the freeze -- see
10392               	; 	' the hfz block there for why.
10393               	; 	' A HIT DOES NOT END A JUMP. This used to force ST_RUN and zero the arc,
10394               	; 	' which dropped him straight down out of mid-air onto whatever he happened
10395               	; 	' to be over -- and since the arc is ballistic and ignores the stick once
10396               	; 	' he is airborne (0l), that read as the game taking the controls away
10397               	; 	' rather than as a hit landing. The penalty is the nine units and the
10398               	; 	' knock flash; where he comes down is still his own arc.
10399               	; 	'

10854               	; 		' this is per-frame code. Two adjacent bits give 0,4,8,12.

10859               	; 		' Harry runs 1.75, so eight frames a pose is 14. Matching the two
10860               	; 		' rates to the two speeds is what keeps both looking like running.

11235               	; 	' cycle's LOW beat bit. IT MUST MOVE WITH THE BEAT BITS ABOVE IT: on the
11236               	; 	' wrong bit he rises and falls twice per stride, a second clock inside one
11237               	; 	' figure, which is the flapping of DESIGN.md 0j2 in the vertical.
11238               	; 	'
11239               	; 	' Safe because HARRY'S COLLISION HAS NO VERTICAL COMPONENT: he is caught on
11240               	; 	' `same level AND |dx| < CATCHR`. Doing this to Kelly would desynchronise
11241               	; 	' his sprite from the ball and biplane windows in DESIGN.md 5a, which is
11242               	; 	' why it is not done to him.
11243               	; 	' THE WHOLE FIGURE RISES, legs included, rather than the body stretching
11244               	; 	' away from the feet. Two reasons, and the second was not the first plan:
11245               	; 	'
11246               	; 	'   * It is what a run does. Mid-flight BOTH feet are off the ground, so
11247               	; 	'     lifting the legs with the body is the correct pose, not a compromise.
11248               	; 	'   * Lifting the body alone opens a one-pixel gap at the waist, and the
11249               	; 	'     torso's bottom row and the legs' top row do not align across it --
11250               	; 	'     green shows through and he reads as coming apart.
11251               	; 	'
11252               	; 	' It also keeps `hfy = hy - 7` and `hy2 = hy + 16` LITERAL, which is not a
11253               	; 	' cosmetic concern: assets/checkbands.py reads each band's draw offset by
11254               	; 	' parsing those exact expressions. Bobbing a differently-named variable
11255               	; 	' made them unreadable and the gate failed the build -- correctly. A
11256               	; 	' checker that can no longer see what it checks has to fail, not shrug.
11257               	; 	' THE RECOVERY LIFT IS A RUNNING THING. Standing on a step he would
11258               	; 	' bob a pixel against a staircase that is itself moving, which reads as

11736               	;
11737               	; 	' ======================================================================
11738               	; 	' THE SCANNER
11739               	; 	' ======================================================================
11740               	; 	' Rows 21-23, 16 chars wide, centred: 48 characters whose PATTERNS are
11741               	; 	' poked directly, so a moving dot costs two writes and no name-table
11742               	; 	' traffic. With the flip (DESIGN.md 2a) this is how you know where Harry
11743               	; 	' is at all -- he can be one pixel off-screen and completely invisible.
11744               	; 	'
11745               	; 	' Rows 21-23 all sit in the THIRD screen third, so every scanner pattern
11746               	; 	' is at base 4096 and no third-selection arithmetic is needed.
11747               	; 	'
11748               	; 	' BOTH DOTS ARE WHITE and Kelly's BLINKS. The manual wants Kelly black
11749               	; 	' and Harry white, but this is the TMS9918's two-colours-per-8x1-cell
11750               	; 	' mode: a black dot and a white dot on the same pixel row of the same
11751               	; 	' character cannot both exist. Blinking distinguishes them with one
11752               	; 	' colour, which is what RallyX does with its player dot.
11753               	; 	' THE STEPS MOVE, AND EVERY ESCALATOR ON SCREEN MOVES WITH THEM. A flight
11754               	; 	' is twelve characters -- six per direction, sliced out of a rendered
11755               	; 	' 64x40 bitmap by genart.py -- so rewriting those twelve PATTERNS animates
11756               	; 	' the lot: 96 bytes, no name-table traffic, and the same cost whether one
11757               	; 	' flight is visible or ten. The phases slide the cells ALONG the slope, so
11758               	; 	' the steps travel up the flight rather than drifting sideways.
11759               	; esc_tick:
11760               cvb_ESC_TICK
11761               	; 	' ONLY SCREENS 0 AND 7 CARRY A FLIGHT, so six screens in eight skip this
11762               	; 	' entirely -- which is what makes rewriting the cells every frame
11763               	; 	' affordable. Nested, not `klsc > 0 AND klsc < 7`: the 9900 backend
11764               	; 	' miscompiles a compare-AND-compare (CLAUDE.md 3A).
11765               	; 	IF klsc > 0 THEN
11766 EB2E D020  34 	movb @cvb_KLSC,r0
     EB30 21A2

     EB34 0100

11784               	; 	' ONE PHASE PER PASS, AND NEVER MORE. There are four phases covering an
11785               	; 	' 8 px period, so advancing by the frame delta ALIASES: at fdv 2 the
11786               	; 	' pattern flips between two positions half a period apart and the
11787               	; 	' direction stops being readable, and at fdv 3 the sequence runs 0,3,2,1
11788               	; 	' -- the staircase visibly runs BACKWARDS, carrying its steps down while
11789               	; 	' the rider goes up. That is the wagon-wheel effect, and no amount of
11790               	; 	' phase arithmetic fixes it: a 4-phase cycle can only be stepped by 1.
11791               	; 	'
11792               	; 	' So the ANIMATION is the clock here, and the rider is paced from it --
11793               	; 	' see move_kelly, which advances him by the same fixed 2-and-1 per pass
11794               	; 	' rather than by fdv. Locking the two together is the only way they
11795               	; 	' cannot drift, and it is what "the player moves at the rate the steps
11796               	; 	' carry him" actually means. The cost is that a ride takes 36 passes
11797               	; 	' rather than 36 frames, so it slows down when the loop does -- which is
11798               	; 	' the honest behaviour for a machine that is carrying you.
11799               	; 	escp = escp + 1

12096               	; 	' ------------------------------------------------- the scanner's furniture
12097               	; 	' Without this the scanner is two dots in a void: you can see THAT Harry is
12098               	; 	' somewhere, but not what he is near, which is the one thing you actually
12099               	; 	' need when he is off-screen. Floor lines say which level, the slashes say
12100               	; 	' where that floor's escalator is, and the bar says where the elevator is --
12101               	; 	' exactly the three things the manual lists.
12102               	; 	'
12103               	; 	' FURNITURE AND DOTS ARE SEGREGATED BY PIXEL ROW ON PURPOSE, and a level
12104               	; 	' band is now FOUR rows, one per colour, because a pixel row carries
12105               	; 	' exactly one colour here:
12106               	; 	'
12107               	; 	'   +0  GREY    escalator head, and the elevator car
12108               	; 	'   +1  GREY    the air of that floor
12109               	; 	'   +2  GREY
12110               	; 	'   +3  YELLOW  the floor line -- and NOTHING else goes here
12111               	; 	'
12112               	; 	' THE FIRST THREE ROWS ARE THE FLOOR'S AIR AND EVERYTHING LIVES IN THEM:
12113               	; 	' the escalator's three-step diagonal, the lift car, and both actors, all
12114               	; 	' three pixels tall. They are grey in the table, and the Kop and the
12115               	; 	' crook recolour their own CHARACTER as they move (scan_mark) -- which is
12116               	; 	' what lets both of them fill the band instead of getting a pixel row
12117               	; 	' each. Eight pixels of this canvas is half a screen of the store, so
12118               	; 	' they are almost never in one character; when they are, they merge.
12119               	; 	'
12120               	; 	' Shrinking from six rows bought eight empty pixel rows, four above the
12121               	; 	' instrument and four below, so it no longer butts against the shop floor
12122               	; 	' above it or the bottom of the screen.
12123               	; 	'
12124               	; 	' The dots are erased by ANDing their bits out, so anything sharing a row
12125               	; 	' with one is rubbed away wherever an actor has passed -- which is why

12470               	; 	' of ROM. This runs twice a game -- at setup and on a new Krook -- so a
12471               	; 	' loop costs nothing anybody can perceive, and it hands the fixed area
12472               	; 	' back the best part of half a kilobyte, which is the budget that
12473               	; 	' actually binds. Paced in bursts: a few hundred VDP writes in a single
12474               	; 	' frame are silently dropped (CLAUDE.md 3A).

12477               	; 	' THIS ADDRESS IS A CHARACTER CODE IN DISGUISE, AND IT WENT STALE.
12478               	; 	' 4096 is the pattern table's BOTTOM THIRD -- rows 16-23, which is
12479               	; 	' band 0 and the radar together -- and the canvas characters begin at
12480               	; 	' genart's SCAN_FIRST, so the base is 4096 + SCAN_FIRST*8. It was
12481               	; 	' written out by hand as 4096 + 160*8 when SCAN_FIRST was 160; art
12482               	; 	' added later moved SCAN_FIRST to 208 and nothing moved this with it,
12483               	; 	' so the wipe zeroed the 48 characters BELOW the canvas and never
12484               	; 	' touched the canvas at all.
12485               	; 	'
12486               	; 	' Two of those forty-eight are STRUCTURE. ENDWALL is the building's
12487               	; 	' outside wall and SLABP is a pillar's cap. Blanking a pattern in ONE
12488               	; 	' THIRD leaves a character that draws correctly everywhere else and
12489               	; 	' falls back to its own background colour here -- so the GROUND FLOOR's
12490               	; 	' outside wall turned into plain green while the identical wall one
12491               	; 	' storey up was perfect, and the ground floor's pillars lost the brick
12492               	; 	' carried up through the bar above them. ENDWALL appears only on
12493               	; 	' screens 0 and 7, which is exactly why it was reported as happening
12494               	; 	' only on the escalator screens, mirrored side to side.
12495               	; 	'
12496               	; 	' The name table was correct the whole time. Probing it said so, four
12497               	; 	' times. It was the GLYPH that was empty, in one third only -- which a
12498               	; 	' probe that copies the character somewhere else to look at it cannot
12499               	; 	' see, because the copy renders from a different third's pattern.
12500               	; 	'

12574               	; 	' That split is what makes the instrument simple. The floor lines, the
12575               	; 	' flights and the lift car do not move relative to the canvas, so they
12576               	; 	' are pixels in the scanner's own characters and cost nothing to keep.
12577               	; 	' The Kop and the crook DO move, and as sprites they need no colour
12578               	; 	' table, no erase and no priority arithmetic -- they draw over the
12579               	; 	' furniture because sprites always do, and nothing shifts to make room.
12580               	; 	'
12581               	; 	' IT ALSO REMOVED THE BLINK. Kelly flashed because a pixel row of this
12582               	; 	' canvas can only carry one colour, so at close range the two markers
12583               	; 	' merged and the blink was the only thing left to tell them apart. Two
12584               	; 	' sprites are two colours wherever they stand.
12585               	; 	'
12586               	; 	' The furniture is drawn ONCE, by scan_furn. It used to be redrawn every
12587               	; 	' tick because erasing a character-based marker ANDed bits out of
12588               	; 	' whatever it was standing on; there is nothing left to rub it away. The
12589               	; 	' car still redraws itself, because the car actually moves.
12590               	; 	' -- the lift car. IT WAS FLICKERING, and the cause was not the drawing
12591               	; 	' but the ERASING: scan_elev cleared its three cells and put them back
12592               	; 	' every tick, whether or not the car had moved, so several times a second
12593               	; 	' there was a window with the pixels off. A sprite has no erase at all --
12594               	; 	' it is placed, and the VDP does the rest -- and slot 26 sits BELOW the

13380               	;
13381               	; 	' THE BONUS IS COUNTED OUT, NOT AWARDED. Dropping the whole sum into the
13382               	; 	' score in one frame tells the player a number; ticking the clock down a
13383               	; 	' unit at a time, with the score climbing and a beat under each step,
13384               	; 	' tells them what the number was FOR. It is the pay-off for every second
13385               	; 	' they saved, and every arcade game of this era spends a moment on it.
13386               	; 	'
13387               	; 	' It also costs nothing to get right: the loop already has to run down
13388               	; 	' `tsec`, so the animation IS the calculation, and the repeated-addition
13389               	; 	' note below stops applying -- each step adds one band's worth.
13390               	; 	'
13391               	; 	' x100 for Krooks 1-9, x200 for 10-15, x300 from 16. Two independent
13392               	; 	' sources agree on those bands; the manual's own wording suggests
13393               	; 	' 1-8 / 9-16 / 17+ and DESIGN.md 0 records the disagreement.
13394               	; 	'
13395               	; 	' #bval MUST BE 16-BIT: 300 does not fit in a byte, and a plain variable
13396               	; 	' would silently truncate it to 44 (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13397               	; bonus_count:
13398               cvb_BONUS_COUNT

13513               	;
13514               	; 	' AND IT ENDS ON ITS LAST BLIP -- there is no closing accent.
13515               	; 	'
13516               	; 	' Two were tried. The bench's own ending for this variant rose a fourth,
13517               	; 	' to 2,542 Hz, and a square wave there is a shriek -- the same fault the
13518               	; 	' pickup was rewritten for. Dropping it an OCTAVE BELOW the ticks, to
13519               	; 	' 518 Hz, was reported the same way, and that one cannot be too high by
13520               	; 	' any measure: it is the lowest note in the effect.
13521               	; 	'
13522               	; 	' So the complaint is not the pitch, it is the extra note. A tally is
13523               	; 	' arithmetic, and arithmetic finishes when the last term is added; a
13524               	; 	' flourish after it is a second event the player has to interpret, and
13525               	; 	' the HUD has already said the clock is empty. The count stops when the
13526               	; 	' counting stops.
13527               	;
13528               	; 	' `calc_bonus` USED TO LIVE HERE and computed the whole sum by repeated
13529               	; 	' addition, to dodge two hazards at once: `tsec * bmul` is an 8-bit
13530               	; 	' product (a 50-unit capture in the x300 band pays 15,000, six times past
13531               	; 	' a byte), and multiplying properly lands on the MPY/r0 hazard where a
13532               	; 	' 16-bit variable read straight after being multiplied returns the
13533               	; 	' product's high word. Counting the bonus out a unit at a time (above)
13534               	; 	' removes the multiply entirely rather than working around it -- the loop
13535               	; 	' the player watches IS the arithmetic.
13536               	; 	'
13537               	; 	' It also fixed the last-tick case for free: `bn_loop` tests `tsec = 0`
13538               	; 	' on entry, where the old `FOR bi = 1 TO tsec` would have run its body
13539               	; 	' once and paid a full multiplier for no time at all (CLAUDE.md 3A).
13540               	;

13694               	;
13695               	; 	' Silence every channel FIRST. SOUND latches, and the per-channel decay
13696               	; 	' counters are not ticked inside this loop -- a tone still sounding when
13697               	; 	' the pause starts would hang for its whole duration, which is the classic
13698               	; 	' CVBasic sticky-audio failure.
13699               	; 	' EVERY CHANNEL OFF, AND THE DECAY COUNTERS WITH THEM. The counters are
13700               	; 	' ticked by the main loop, so anything still sounding when the loop stops
13701               	; 	' -- for a capture, a death, the bonus count -- sustains for as long as
13702               	; 	' whatever replaced the loop takes. That is where the long beep over the
13703               	; 	' bonus tally came from: not the tally's own note, which turns itself off
13704               	; 	' after every unit, but a footstep or a hit that was still ringing when

13711               	; 	' NOISE channel. So a step ringing when Harry was caught was never turned

14072               	; 	' THE JUMP IS A WARBLE, NOT A SWEEP -- testsounds variant A, measured off
14073               	; 	' the 2600 at about 415 Hz alternating with 188 for roughly 280 ms.

14078               	; 	' does. Eight ticks alternating is four cycles of warble, which is what the
14079               	; 	' recording shows.

14141               	;
14142               	; 	' THE LOW-TIME WARNING IS SILENT. There was a beep a second under ten, and
14143               	; 	' it was the wrong instrument for the job: the last ten seconds are the
14144               	; 	' busiest part of a round, so a repeating tone arrives exactly when the
14145               	; 	' player most needs to hear the hazards, and it fought the prize arpeggio
14146               	; 	' for channel 2 as well. The flash says the same thing and says it in the
14147               	; 	' place the player is already looking.
14148               	;
14149               	; 	' FOOTSTEPS ARE NOISE, AND ON THE NOISE CHANNEL -- testsounds variant A.
14150               	; 	'
14151               	; 	' They were two alternating TONES on channel 0, which is neither what the
14152               	; 	' original does nor a good use of a channel: the recording says a footstep
14153               	; 	' is a short burst of white noise, and channel 3 was sitting unused while
14154               	; 	' the footsteps and the jump sweep shared channel 0 and had to take turns.
14155               	; 	'
14156               	; 	' TESTSOUNDS RUN D: a SHORT tick at the measured RATE.
14157               	; 	'
14158               	; 	' The two dials are independent and both were tried at the bench. The
14159               	; 	' 2600 plays a 64 ms burst every 165 ms -- six a second -- and variant A
14160               	; 	' copies both. Ten a second was tried on the way here and reads as
14161               	; 	' hurrying rather than running. What D changes is not the cadence but the
14162               	; 	' TICK: two frames rather than four, and a notch louder to carry at half
14163               	; 	' the length. Same six a second, less of it.
14164               	; 	'
14165               	; 	' EIGHT A SECOND, AND THE ACCUMULATOR NOW CARRIES ITS REMAINDER.
14166               	; 	'
14167               	; 	' sfw counted pixels and the trigger did `sfw = 0`, THROWING AWAY whatever
14168               	; 	' was past the threshold. kspd is about four pixels a pass, so a threshold
14169               	; 	' of 17 did not fire at 17 -- it fired at the first multiple past it, about
14170               	; 	' 20, and every rate this was ever set to came out slower than the number
14171               	; 	' said: the "six a second" was 5.2 and the "ten" that read as hurrying was
14172               	; 	' really 8.7. Subtracting the threshold instead keeps the fraction, so the
14173               	; 	' rate is what it claims to be at any walking speed.
14174               	; 	'
14175               	; 	' 104 px/s over 15 px is 6.9 a second -- between the 8.0 that read as
14176               	; 	' slightly hurried and the 6.1 that read as trudging. The dial is this one
14177               	; 	' constant and the subtraction below, which must stay threshold + 1 or the
14178               	; 	' carry is wrong.
14179               	; 	'
14180               	; 	' SOT = 2 IS THE SHORTEST TICK THERE IS, and 1 is SILENCE. The decay block
14181               	; 	' below runs LATER IN THE SAME sfx_tick, so a count of 1 is decremented to
14182               	; 	' zero on the pass that set it and the note-off fires before the sound has
14183               	; 	' lasted any time at all. 2 survives to the next pass, which is one pass of
14184               	; 	' sound -- about 42 ms against the bench's 33, as close as a per-pass timer
14185               	; 	' gets, and the reason the bench and the game cannot sound identical.
14186               	; 	'
14187               	; 	' Register 4 is white noise at the fastest rate.
14188               	; 	'
14189               	; 	' VOLUME 9, WHICH IS UNDER EVERYTHING ELSE ON PURPOSE. The hit, the prize
14190               	; 	' and the jump are 12 and 13, and they happen ONCE; footsteps play for the
14191               	; 	' whole round. At 13 they were level with the events they are supposed to
14192               	; 	' sit beneath, so the effects that carry information had nothing to stand
14193               	; 	' out from. The tone version was 7 for the same reason -- noise does read
14194               	; 	' quieter than a tone at the same number, which is why this is 9 and not
14195               	; 	' back to 7.
14196               	; 	IF sfw > 14 THEN
14197 FBAA D020  34 	movb @cvb_SFW,r0
     FBAC 2210

     FBB0 0F00

     FBB8 FBF0

     FBC0 F100

14319               	;
14320               	; 	' EVERYTHING BELOW THIS LINE IS ASSEMBLED INTO BANK 1, so the INCLUDE order
14321               	; 	' is load-bearing and nothing but data may follow it.
14322               	; 	'
14323               	; 	' THE FONT IS NOW IN THE BANK TOO, and it used to be deliberately outside:
14324               	; 	' keeping one readable thing in bank 0 means a bank-selection mistake shows
14325               	; 	' as "text survives, art does not" rather than a uniformly blank screen,
14326               	; 	' which is a genuinely useful thing to have when a bank goes wrong.
14327               	; 	'
14328               	; 	' THE FONT HAS A BANK OF ITS OWN, and the reason is not its size.
14329               	; 	'
14330               	; 	' Bank 1 was FULL -- six spare bytes of 8,192 -- which shut the door on
14331               	; 	' moving anything else out of the fixed area, and the fixed area is the
14332               	; 	' only budget that cannot be grown (linkticart writes exactly three
14333               	; 	' loader pages and discards the rest; they are the 32K expansion's RAM at
14334               	; 	' >A000, not cart ROM). A second bank costs a bigger cart -- five pages
14335               	; 	' round up to eight, so 32 KB becomes 64 KB -- and buys back the ability
14336               	; 	' to keep evacuating data out of code.
14337               	; 	'
14338               	; 	' THE FONT IS THE RIGHT TENANT because it is read ONCE. Two DEFINEs copy
14339               	; 	' it into VRAM at setup and nothing looks at it again, so it is the only
14340               	; 	' block here that can sit on a page which is not permanently mapped. See
14341               	; 	' setup_font: bank 2 is selected for those two statements and bank 1 for
14342               	; 	' the whole of the rest of the program.
14343               	; 	'
14344               	; 	' EVERYTHING ELSE STAYS IN BANK 1, because everything else is read during
14345               	; 	' play -- art on a screen crossing, templates on a band blit, the lookup
14346               	; 	' tables every pass. One permanently-mapped bank for all of it means
14347               	; 	' there is no switch to miss.
14348               	; 	#if TI994A
14349               	; 	BANK 2
14350      0354     BANK_0_FREE:	EQU >fffe-$
     **** ****     > .rept

14488               	;
14489               	; 	' THE COLOUR TABLE, 472 bytes of the same value ($14 = black ink on dark blue).
14490               	; 	'
14491               	; 	' Loaded with DEFINE COLOR 32,59,font_col, which is ONE synchronous call that
14492               	; 	' writes all three screen thirds (define_color always does the LDIRVM3 triple
14493               	; 	' copy). It replaced a VPOKE loop that wrote this one value 1,416 times paced by
14494               	; 	' 24 WAITs -- the largest scripted delay in the boot, and the reason the title
14495               	; 	' screen used to fill in visibly rather than appearing at once.
14496               	; 	'
14497               	; 	' EIGHT BYTES PER CHARACTER, not one. Supply fewer and DEFINE COLOR reads
14498               	; 	' whatever follows in ROM as colour data, with no error at build or run time.
14499               	;

14501               cvb_FONT_COL

14621               	; 	' ==================================================
14622               	; 	' THE TITLE'S DISPLAY FACE -- 16x16 letters
14623               	; 	' Generated by assets/gentitle.py from titleface.py.
14624               	; 	' Do not edit here; edit the glyphs and rebuild.
14625               	; 	'
14626               	; 	' Four characters per letter: TL TR BL BR, in the order
14627               	; 	' A E K N O P R S T Y
14628               	; 	'
14629               	; 	' IN TWO PIECES, because the character table has no run
14630               	; 	' long enough -- see titleface.FREE_RUNS. setup_font must
14631               	; 	' load them with EXACTLY these arguments:
14632               	; 	'     DEFINE CHAR  182,26,tfont_pat0
14633               	; 	'     DEFINE COLOR 182,26,tfont_col0
14634               	; 	'     DEFINE CHAR    0,14,tfont_pat1
14635               	; 	'     DEFINE COLOR   0,14,tfont_col1
14636               	; 	'
14637               	; 	' LIVES IN BANK 2 -- read once by those DEFINEs, never
14638               	; 	' during play.
14639               	; 	' ==================================================

15010               	; 	' Keystone Kapers art -- GENERATED by assets/genart.py. Do not edit; regenerate.
15011               	; 	'
15012               	; 	' EVERY SPRITE IS 16x16: sprite size and magnification are GLOBAL on the
15013               	; 	' TMS9918, so small objects are drawn small INSIDE a 16x16 box rather than
15014               	; 	' being small sprites.
15015               	; 	'
15016               	; 	' EVERY 8-PX OBJECT SITS IN ROWS 8-15 OF ITS BOX, ducked Kelly included, so
15017               	; 	' one rule places them all: bottom edge = y + 16, and a thing resting on the
15018               	; 	' floor is at y = FLOORY - 16.
15019               	; 	'
15020               	; 	' Sprite bytes are QUADRANT-ORDERED: 16 rows of the left half, then 16 of
15021               	; 	' the right. Every block is an EVEN number of bytes -- an odd DATA BYTE run
15022               	; 	' silently misaligns every word table after it (CLAUDE.md 3A).
15023               	;
15024               	; spr_kelly:	' Kelly: RIGHT hat/face/tunic/tunic-arm-up/duck-hat/duck-face, then the same LEFT (+24), then the FOUR shared run frames. Patterns 0..60
15025               cvb_SPR_KELLY

16256               	; 	INCLUDE "store.bas"
16257               	; 	' Keystone Kapers store -- GENERATED by assets/genstore.py. Do not edit.
16258               	; 	'
16259               	; 	' EIGHT band templates of 5 rows x 32 cols (160 bytes each) plus a 32-byte
16260               	; 	' index over (level, screen). The whole 8-screen, 4-level building is about
16261               	; 	' 1.3 KB instead of the 5,120 bytes it would cost to store literally.
16262               	; 	'
16263               	; 	' All eight templates are ONE contiguous block under ONE label, so a band
16264               	; 	' blit is
16265               	; 	'     SCREEN stor_tpl, tpl*160, toprow*32, 32, 5, 32
16266               	; 	' with no label ladder -- SCREEN needs a literal label and a label cannot be
16267               	; 	' chosen by a variable, which is why RallyX needed a 4-way IF over its maze
16268               	; 	' tables. One block sidesteps it.
16269               	; 	'
16270               	; 	' 160 is EVEN, so this cannot leave the location counter odd and misalign
16271               	; 	' the word tables defined after it.
16272               	; 	'
16273               	; 	' template ids:
16274               	; 	'   0 T_AISLE_A
16275               	; 	'   1 T_AISLE_B
16276               	; 	'   2 T_ESC_W
16277               	; 	'   3 T_ESC_E
16278               	; 	'   4 T_ELEV
16279               	; 	'   5 T_ROOF0
16280               	; 	'   6 T_ROOF1
16281               	; 	'   7 T_ROOF2
16282               	; 	'   8 T_ROOF3
16283               	; 	'   9 T_ROOF4
16284               	; 	'   10 T_ROOF5
16285               	; 	'   11 T_ROOF6
16286               	; 	'   12 T_ROOF7
16287               	; 	'   13 T_END_W
16288               	; 	'   14 T_END_E
16289               	;
16290               	; stor_tpl:	' 15 templates x 160 bytes
